back: A person outside their country of nationality who cannot or will not return because of a well-founded fear of persecution (race, religion, nationality, social group or political opinion).
Asylum seeker: has applied for protection and awaits a decision. IDP: forced to flee but remains inside their own country.
Internal or international; voluntary or forced; permanent, temporary, seasonal or circular; skilled or unskilled; documented or undocumented.

front: Share of the world's people who are international migrants?
back: About 3.6% (about 280 million in 2020, United Nations, rounded).
Most migrants move short distances; step migration; every flow has a counter-flow; economic motives dominate; rural people migrate more than urban people.
Push factors at the origin, pull factors at the destination, intervening obstacles (distance, cost, laws) and personal factors.
Flow $\propto \dfrac{P_1 \times P_2}{d^2}$: large, near places attract the most migrants.

front: Main destination of labour migrants in southern Africa?
back: South Africa (mines, farms, cities), with workers from Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Malawi and Lesotho; Botswana is also a destination.
Emigration of skilled and educated people such as nurses and teachers, which weakens the source country.
